detail.summary: This revised synthesis examines how aggregate performance gains in multi-agent debate and consensus paradigms can conceal selective hidden-task degradation, and incorporates evidence regarding self-reference and structural limits in consensus formation.

detail.title: Epistemic Reliability and Consensus Limitations in Multi-Agent Systems
detail.summary: This synthesis examines how aggregate performance gains in multi-agent debate and consensus paradigms can conceal selective hidden-task degradation, raising questions about blindly trusting group consensus over verifiable individual reliability.
detail.reason: Synthesizing collected evidence to evaluate consensus reliability versus independent epistemic monitoring.
